title: Aadhaar — building identity as public infrastructure
statement: Nilekani left Infosys co-chairmanship to build UIDAI, arguing that a biometric identity number could become the pipe infrastructure of Indian public life.
outcome: Aadhaar enrolled over a billion people, became the world's largest biometric ID system, and seeded the India Stack — UPI payments, DBT transfers — that digitized the Indian economy.

title: Returning to Infosys as chairman in the crisis
statement: After a board-level governance collapse and CEO exit, Nilekani returned as non-executive chairman to stabilize the company he co-founded, at a moment of maximal uncertainty.
outcome: He appointed Salil Parekh as CEO, restored client and investor confidence, and stepped back in 2022 with the company at record scale.

title: Funding and chairing the EkStep foundation
statement: Nilekani and wife Rohini founded EkStep to build open digital learning infrastructure, applying the platform philosophy of Aadhaar to primary literacy.
outcome: EkStep's open-source approach influenced India's DIKSHA education platform reaching hundreds of millions of students.
